title: Slack admin, SSO and app changes
volume: None on a normal day for roles and SSO. App scopes change when apps update, a few a month.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for Slack, on the CloudAudit records the library's Slack parsers write from the Audit Logs API. They make a detection when a member is made an admin or owner, the SSO or two-factor setting changes, or an app's scopes expand. Each rule matches sensor type Slack Audit Logs only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Slack parsers and the example bridge in bridges/slack-audit-logs, and run the bridge with an Enterprise organization's audit logs token, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write Slack's action, such as role_change_to_admin, as the event name, the actor as the user and a user entity as the target user.
- The SSO rule takes every change to the SSO setting or two-factor requirement; the previous and new values are in request_parameters, so check which way it went.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 6 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 21 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only a sample sign-in on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The events went in through bridges/slack-audit-logs, run once on the lab machine against a local mock of the Slack Audit Logs API that served the sample events, and posted to HTTP Ingest as gzipped NDJSON, the way the bridge's README says.

Known gaps:
- The bridge polls, so detections arrive up to one poll interval after the event.
- Slack audit logs need an Enterprise plan, so these rules don't work on Pro or Business+ workspaces.
